answers.explain: 'Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.'
'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.'
Simon, a Galilean fisherman from Bethsaida living at Capernaum, was brought to Jesus by his brother Andrew and renamed Cephas, 'Rock' (Peter).
'That they may all be one': Christ's prayer for the unity of the Church.
Hebrew for 'adversary', the tempter defeated by Christ.
Jesus took bread, blessed it and said 'This is my body': the Eucharist.
A song from the Book of Psalms; one is sung at every Mass after the first reading.
'He is not here, for he has risen.' The heart of the Gospel.
The mountain where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments.
The twelve tribes of Israel, descended from the sons of Jacob.
The table of sacrifice where the Eucharist is offered; it stands for Christ himself at the center of the church.
The consecrated Host is the Body of Christ; 'Lord God of hosts' means God of the heavenly armies.
Bread from heaven that fed Israel in the desert, a sign of the Eucharist.
Judah's exile in Babylon, and our life on earth 'in this valley of tears'.
Our Lady of Guadalupe left roses in Juan Diego's tilma; roses are a Marian symbol.
'A royal priesthood': the priesthood of all the baptized.
'Peace I leave with you': the sign of peace is exchanged before Communion.
A spiritual creature who serves God as messenger; every believer has a guardian angel (CCC 336).
The white baptismal garment: 'you have clothed yourselves with Christ'.
The Sermon on the Mount: the Beatitudes.
'This my son was dead and is alive again': the prodigal son.
The fallen angel who tempted Jesus in the desert.
David, youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, was a shepherd anointed by Samuel, who killed Goliath, served and fled from Saul, and became king first of Judah at Hebron and then of all Israel.
The tower of human pride; Pentecost reverses its confusion of tongues.
Thomas would not believe until he saw the mark of the nails.
'My sheep hear my voice': Christ is the Good Shepherd.
'Your kingdom come': the Kingdom of God is the center of Jesus' preaching.
Israel's land of slavery, and later the Holy Family's refuge.
'I am the light of the world': the Easter candle is lit from the new fire.
'Woman, behold your son': Jesus gives Mary to the beloved disciple.
Placed on the forehead on Ash Wednesday: 'Remember that you are dust.'
Seven sacraments, seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, seven deadly sins.
The star went before the Magi until it stopped over the place where the child was.
The theological virtue by which we believe God and all he has revealed.
A day of celebration in the Church's calendar, ranked below a solemnity.
To call down God's favor; the priest blesses the people at the end of Mass.
Gold, frankincense and myrrh: myrrh foreshadowed his burial.
'I am the vine, you are the branches.'
Elder brother of Moses, appointed by God as his spokesman before Pharaoh.
'Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies…'
The successors of Peter as Bishop of Rome.
The rosary is prayed on beads: five decades of Hail Marys.
Prayer is 'the raising of one's mind and heart to God' (CCC 2559).
The long narrow vestment worn by priests and deacons, a sign of ordained ministry.
Baptism is new birth 'of water and the Spirit'.
The younger twin of Isaac and Rebekah, who bought Esau's birthright and, with his mother's help, received Isaac's blessing.
Solomon built the Temple with cedars of Lebanon.
'For by grace you have been saved through faith.'
To worship God alone; Eucharistic adoration is prayer before the Blessed Sacrament.
'Put on the whole armor of God' to stand against evil.
'The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.'
Lent is a season of prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
The crown of thorns pressed on Jesus' head in the Passion.
The Kingdom of heaven is like yeast leavening the whole loaf.
Ravens fed Elijah by the brook Cherith.
A tenth of one's increase given to God; Abraham gave a tithe to Melchizedek.
'The sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.'
A physical remain of a saint, honored as a sign of the resurrection.
Songs of praise; St Paul urges the Church to sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs.
'Create in me a clean heart, O God.'
Levite born in Egypt under Pharaoh's death-decree, drawn from the Nile and raised by Pharaoh's daughter.
Christ the King is honored on the last Sunday of the Church year.
The Kingdom of heaven is like a merchant who finds one pearl of great price.
'I am the way, and the truth, and the life.'
A holy one in heaven; the Church canonizes some as models and intercessors.
Jesus called fishermen from their boats to be fishers of men.
From the Latin credo, 'I believe': the Nicene Creed is professed at Sunday Mass.
The sign of our salvation, traced over ourselves at the start of every prayer.
The flood in Noah's day is a figure of Baptism (1 Pet 3:20-21).
'He will come again to judge the living and the dead.'
Jesus told Peter, 'Feed my lambs': the shepherd's charge of the pope.
God's love that forgives; the Sunday after Easter is Divine Mercy Sunday.
The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone.
The widow's two small coins gave more than all the rest.
Easter morning the women found the tomb empty.
Singers who lead the assembly's song; the area of the church where they sing.
The Gloria, the angels' hymn at Christ's birth, is sung on Sundays outside Advent and Lent.
From the Greek for 'the books': the Catholic Bible has 73 of them.
The Spirit descended on Jesus like a dove at his baptism.
Gregorian chant is the Church's own music, given 'pride of place' by Vatican II.
The Magi, traditionally three kings, came to worship the newborn King.
Jesus cast out demons as a sign that the Kingdom had come.
A watch on the eve of a feast; the Easter Vigil is 'the mother of all vigils'.
God's free gift of his own life, poured into the soul through the sacraments.
The son of the promise, born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age and named 'laughter'.
The Sacred Heart of Jesus, symbol of his love, is honored in June.
Sacred images that are 'windows to heaven' in Eastern tradition.
Mid-afternoon prayer, at the hour Jesus died.
Fourth son of Jacob and Leah.
Twin son of Judah and Tamar who 'broke through' ahead of his brother Zerah at birth; father of Hezron and Hamul.
Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham as a wife so that Sarah might have children through her.
Nabal ('fool'), a rich and surly man of Maon with flocks at Carmel, insulted David's men; after Abigail's intercession he was struck by the LORD and died.
Titus was a Greek convert and trusted co-worker of Paul.
Hiram (Huram) king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's palace and made a treaty with Solomon, supplying cedar, cypress and skilled workers for the Temple in exchange for grain and oil.
Devotion and reverence toward God; one of the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit.

Silas, a leading man and prophet of the Jerusalem church, was sent with Judas Barsabbas to bring the Council's letter to Antioch, and then chosen by Paul as companion on the second missionary journey.
The nave is the main body of a church where the people gather (from navis, 'ship').
Wife of Elimelech of Bethlehem.
The tall pointed hat worn by a bishop.
Presbyter, the Greek word behind 'priest', means 'elder'.
Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours.
An Israelite of the tribe of Naphtali deported to Nineveh, Tobit remained faithful to the Law, gave generous alms and risked his life to bury executed fellow Jews.
Heman son of Joel, grandson of the prophet Samuel, of the Korahite clan of Kohath, was one of David's three chief Temple musicians and 'the king's seer'.
A white linen cloth a priest may wear around the neck under the alb.
Eldest son of Aaron.
Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, was the father of Jeroboam I, who is constantly called 'Jeroboam the son of Nebat'.
Wife and half-sister of Abraham, long barren.
Zadok son of Ahitub, a priest descended from Eleazar son of Aaron, served alongside Abiathar under David and carried the Ark when David fled Absalom.
Uriah the Hittite, one of David's Thirty mighty men, refused to go home to his wife while the Ark and army were in the field.
Jonah son of Amittai, from Gath-hepher, prophesied in the time of Jeroboam II.
Son of Jared in the line of Seth and father of Methuselah.

Tamar, David's beautiful daughter and Absalom's full sister, was raped by her half-brother Amnon and then cast out; she lived desolate in Absalom's house, and his revenge set off the tragedies of David's later reign.
The realm of the dead; Christ descended there to free the just (CCC 633).
Abner son of Ner, Saul's kinsman (his cousin according to 1 Sam 14:50-51), commanded Saul's army and after Saul's death made Ishbosheth king over Israel.
A monastery led by an abbot or abbess, such as the Benedictines of Monte Cassino.
Rebekah's brother in Haran, who welcomed Abraham's servant and later Jacob.
Son of Zippor and king of Moab, who, afraid of Israel camped on the plains of Moab, summoned Balaam to curse them.
Second son of Aaron.
Amnon, David's firstborn, became obsessed with his half-sister Tamar, raped her by a ruse and then hated her.
Asaph son of Berechiah, a Levite of the Gershonite line, was appointed by David as chief of the Temple singers with cymbals.
Amorite king ruling from Heshbon who refused Israel passage through his land and attacked them; Israel defeated him and took his territory east of the Jordan, which Moses gave to Reuben and Gad.
Son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, the spy from Judah who, with Joshua, urged Israel to trust God and take the land.
The Hivite prince of the land at Shechem, from whose sons Jacob bought a field.
Bethlehemite, son of Obed and grandson of Boaz and Ruth, father of eight sons, the youngest of whom, David, was anointed king by Samuel.
A chamber beneath a church, often holding the relics of saints.
Son of Hammedatha (called 'the Bugaean', and in the Greek letter 'the Macedonian'), exalted above all the king's princes.
Son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, called by Deborah to lead ten thousand men against Sisera.
The Church's liturgical rites: Roman, Byzantine, Maronite and more, all Catholic.

Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, conquered Babylon in 539 BC and issued the decree allowing the Jews to return home and rebuild the Temple, sending back the sacred vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken.
The list of inspired books; also the Eucharistic Prayer (the Roman Canon).
A gathering of bishops to advise the pope or govern a region.
The Passover meal; the Last Supper took place in the setting of Passover.
Levite, son of Izhar and cousin of Moses and Aaron.
A member of a mendicant order such as the Franciscans or Dominicans.
